title: Factorise a non-monic quadratic with a negative middle coefficient

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give your answer in factorised form.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The constant is positive and the middle term is negative, so both bracket constants should be negative.
Check the middle products: -8x and -x combine to -9x.

hint_ladder.title: What do the signs tell you?
hint_ladder.prompt: A positive constant with a negative middle term means the bracket constants should share a negative direction.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Set the first terms to match the leading term, then try factor pairs of the constant while checking the cross-products.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students choose the right constants but use positive signs. Check whether the cross-products create a negative middle term.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For ax^2 + bx + c, use expansion as a test: the two cross-products must combine to bx exactly. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is including the leading coefficient in the brackets.
The stuck point is using two negative constants to create a negative middle term.

mark_scheme_notes: Award method credit for correct first-term structure and full credit for (2x - 1)(x - 4).
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: positive signs despite a negative middle term, weak middle-term checking.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how will the middle term help you choose signs?
